- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 5–7 days) prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–2% for final 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag in sentiment direction.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence to recent 7-day average.
